html:
ForgeMCP 0.2.17 — Landscape baseline delta check

Checked October 24, 2026. Final classification: BLOCKED — SPECIFIC PRESERVATION RISK. The right riverbed extension differs from its approved, saved two-operation height baseline at 24 vertices. No cause or damage diagnosis is inferred. This was a read-only comparison; no preview, sculpt, save, restore, Editor launch, plugin change, or Trello update occurred.

Exact delta and provenance

The current operational inspection authenticated production Editor unreal-33500 / PID 33500, UE 5.6.1, ForgeMCP 0.2.17-alpha.1, correct project/world and PIE stopped. It returned Landscape GUID BD45FDD94EC2A29617B50794F2DE4E9D, Original Layer MD5 9f43572fbc2c06ef497da015879cdb23, ForgeTerrain MD5 f5a8d55a3372fefe6fcadb0e7ff25b07, minimum -100 cm, 16 loaded proxies and 64/64 registered terrain/collision components. The complete 1,192-package loaded inventory found no dirty production Content; only compiled-in /Script/SlateCore was dirty.

The approved two-sculpt execution [not indexed] records a left write rectangle [1043,1068,1057,1074] and a right rectangle [1083,1066,1097,1072], both apply_heightmap on ForgeTerrain under the same locally approved session. They changed 60 vertices each, preserving 101 older carved samples. The right operation's final full-height MD5 was 08cbe382a59441d8148a674cf0d83851; its bounded [1042,1065,1098,1075] MD5 was 3817bd2c18535a9b4529387de493f2b9. The manual-save report [not indexed] established save-log/file-write evidence for the affected packages, but not independent deserialization.

Comparing the 627 actual current native samples with Stage2E_Alpha_20261024T001332Z/expected_reload_baseline.json found 603 identical and 24 different. All 24 are x=1085–1096 on y=1070–1071: the last two nonzero rows of the right extension's saved carve now read 0 cm. The previous values on row 1070 ranged from -1.5625 to -26.5625 cm; row 1071 ranged from -0.78125 to -8.59375 cm. They lie strictly inside the right approved write rectangle, not the left rectangle or the 101 earlier carved samples. Within this bounded region, the left extension, the other 36 of 60 changed right-extension samples, and all 101 pre-existing carved samples retain their recorded values. The bounded current MD5 is 0bce98df53283065e7a173d2d0c56d73. The full-layer MD5 also differs, so other height changes outside this 627-sample region are possible; they were not localized by this check.

Confirmed: the 24 current edit-layer heights differ; the previously authorized right operation created their negative baseline; the existing riverbed still reaches -100 cm; Original Layer identity/hash and proxy/component registration match. Expected only if separately documented: a later intentional rework may have flattened these rows. Unexplained: the operation, person or save that changed them, and any differences elsewhere implied by the full-layer hash. This is a preservation risk, not proof of corruption or a request to restore the old values.

Disk and checkpoint boundary

The affected production proxy Content/__ExternalActors__/Levels/L_City_World_Master/5/K5/KSDE1ZCJBZNOS07IF93SI2.uasset currently hashes SHA-256 40fe8daa2c0a88bbea0e9cc33a97ec639dc99b53a2c23d673febb46c0047fd3d, 610,905 bytes, last write 2026-10-24T01:55:36.2133544Z; its October 23 post-sculpt hash was 01bcd92c87e93b000811a863b88701ec845ff0e7487c868f0ccb92a46a955b61, 609,966 bytes. The root actor file retains SHA-256 9455276756f9b78c36e6c7fc732cadf4b3a486ab9d2237c81917d4677e3022df. These facts show a later disk-file change, not which serialized height values it contains. Current Editor memory and clean flags are not independent disk-reload proof.

The native multi-sculpt checkpoint Saved/ForgeLandscapeAdoption/E1E328994273443311FB4A880BC326BE/manifest.json still exists and hashes SHA-256 f77b772e73774f1516b9fb94ecfd73584ccffa482ecabd92bc92e400a9181ed5, matching the execution report's manifest pin. The Stage 2E expected baseline remains accessible. Only existence and the manifest pin were rechecked here; backup-file payloads and other historical checkpoints were not rehashed. No restoration was performed.

Existing evidence does not locate or characterize the two additional indentations. The changed 24 vertices are one rectangular portion of the right riverbed extension, not proof that those two indentations are present or absent. Their owner-intended coordinates and expected heights need to be supplied or established by an authorized bounded readback comparison before assigning them a preservation verdict.

Mountain-and-valley preview and readiness

The callable unreal_preview_landscape schema supports bounded raise and lower, with a native reviewed preview preceding any apply. A connected production World Partition preview also enforces local editing-session scope; the earlier approval is historical, and this task authorizes no new request or grant. Because the current baseline is unresolved and the indentations' locations are unknown, an unused region and its protective halo cannot be proven. No preview was executed. A preview's safety and numerical predictions therefore remain unverified in this session.

A candidate after resolution is a bounded flat region centered near vertex (1500,1500), far from the known riverbed rectangle; it is unapproved and not yet shown free of the two indentations. Proposed ridge footprint [1440,1470,1560,1530] (121 × 61 vertices) would use several adjacent raise previews with a smooth longitudinal crest, approximately +60 to +180 cm above the current ForgeTerrain layer, and guard rings outside the footprint. A connected valley could occupy [1460,1520,1540,1580] with a shallow lower target of approximately -20 to -60 cm, meeting the ridge through a reviewed transition. These are design targets, not native preview output or approved height samples. A later plan should use fresh bounded reads to choose exact rectangles, operation arrays/falloff and halo, then verify proxy ownership and no overlap with the indentations.

For a controlled test, first resolve the current height intent and make a new immutable, hash-verified production checkpoint. Then use unreal_inspect_landscape and unreal_read_landscape_height_region; obtain unreal_landscape_edit_session_preflight for the exact Landscape, ForgeTerrain layer, actions, regions and current Editor PID; review native unreal_preview_landscape results. A separate local owner approval is needed before applying any raise/lower operation. Verify every changed vertex and guard ring, Original Layer hash, dirty-package scope, 16 proxies, 64/64 components and actual collision behavior. Saving requires separate exact-package owner authorization; preserve logs and recovery files, do not use unrestricted Save All or automatic rollback. Independent disk persistence requires a separately authorized isolated Editor launch after a verified saved-source copy, private writable paths and one-attempt process controls. The earlier Stage 2E approval is consumed and its TedsOutliner startup assertion remains an unproven interactive-startup workaround.

Minimum next authorization/decision: the owner must establish whether flattening the 24 right-extension vertices was intended and identify the two indentations' bounds and expected shape. If intentional, record a new protected baseline and verify its saved files before a mountain/valley preview. If unintended, authorize a separate preservation/recovery review; this report does not recommend automatic restoration. The mountain-and-valley creation test is not ready while the protected right-extension baseline is disputed and disk-backed persistence remains unproved.
